subject: Numeracy
title: Counting and tallying
objectives: Children will make tally marks and count them.
Children will count to 20 with support.
content: Tally marks, counting in fives and tens, and counting games.
teachingActivities: Introduce tally marks through a real need such as counting votes or visitors; draw four lines and a cross-line for five; count in fives along tally groups; use a hundred-square or number line for counting to 20; play counting games to build fluency.
learnerActivities: Make tally marks for up to 5 and count to 20 with support.
assessment: Observe whether each child makes tally marks for up to 5 and counts to 20 with support.
expectedOutcomes: Makes tally marks for up to 5.

lessons.title: Tally marks
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will make tally marks to count things.
successCriteria: Makes tally marks for up to 5
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 15, order numbers and use ordinal words.
lessons.starter: Drop balls into a basket one at a time and say "Let us make a mark each time. These are tally marks."
teacherActivities: Show how to draw one line for each ball.
Show the fifth line crossing the four.
Let children tally another action such as jumps.
learnerActivities: Children watch and draw a line.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to draw one line for each ball. Children: Children watch and draw a line.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the fifth line crossing the four. Children: Children copy the cross-line.
Step 3. Teacher: Count the marks in fives. Children: Children count the marks.
Step 4. Teacher: Let children tally another action such as jumps. Children: Child tallies jumps.

practical.title: Mark and count
practical.safety: Use chalk outdoors or on boards and wash hands afterwards. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Tally to three and count the marks together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tally to ten.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Makes tally marks for up to five
lessons.homeConnection: Tally how many cars you see on a walk.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make tally marks to count things" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Counting in fives
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will count groups of five using tally marks and fingers.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 15, order numbers and use ordinal words.
lessons.starter: Show a hand and say "One hand is five. Two hands are ten."
teacherActivities: Count five counters in a group and say five.
Put another five and say ten.
Check by counting one by one.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Count five counters in a group and say five. Children: Children say five.
Step 2. Teacher: Put another five and say ten. Children: Children say ten.
Step 3. Teacher: Count tally groups in fives. Children: Children count five, ten, fifteen.
Step 4. Teacher: Check by counting one by one. Children: Child counts one by one.

practical.title: Fives and tens
practical.safety: Use large counters and supervise closely. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count to fifty in fives.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many in two groups of five?
What comes after ten in fives?

lessons.conclusion: Put the counters away and say fives.
lessons.homeConnection: Count your fingers and toes in fives.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count groups of five using tally marks and fingers" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Counting to twenty
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will say the numbers from 1 to 20 in order with support.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 15, order numbers and use ordinal words.
lessons.starter: Walk along a number line to 20 and say "Let us count to twenty together."
teacherActivities: Count to 20 with a drum beat.
Say "Well done, you can count to twenty."
learnerActivities: Children count ten then ten more.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Count to 20 with a drum beat. Children: Children count with the beat.
Step 2. Teacher: Count 20 counters in two tens. Children: Children count ten then ten more.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children count in pairs. Children: Pairs count to twenty.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Well done, you can count to twenty." Children: Children clap and cheer.

practical.title: Walk to twenty
practical.safety: Keep the number line flat and secured. Walk slowly and one at a time.

differentiation.support: Count to fifteen with the number line.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count backwards from ten.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Count to twenty together and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Count up to twenty during daily routines.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say the numbers from 1 to 20 in order with support" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Counting games
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will play games that practise counting, tallying and numerals.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 15, order numbers and use ordinal words.
lessons.starter: Show a dice and say "We will throw the dice and count the dots."
teacherActivities: Show how to throw the dice and count the dots.
Let each child throw the dice and collect counters.
Make a tally of the dice throws.
Count the counters at the end.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to throw the dice and count the dots. Children: Children watch and count.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child throw the dice and collect counters. Children: Child throws and counts.
Step 3. Teacher: Make a tally of the dice throws. Children: Child makes a tally mark.
Step 4. Teacher: Count the counters at the end. Children: Child counts the counters.

practical.title: Dice and count
practical.safety: Use large foam dice and keep play on a mat so that nothing rolls away. Supervise turns closely.

differentiation.support: Use a dice with up to three dots.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to add two dice.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the games away and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a dice game at home and count the dots.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "play games that practise counting, tallying and numerals" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 5 tally check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child tallies and counts to twenty.
successCriteria: Makes tally marks for up to 5
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can count to 15, order numbers and use ordinal words.
lessons.starter: Sing the counting song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: tally, fives and dice game.
At each station ask "How many?" and watch.
Record each child’s level and highest number counted.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: tally, fives and dice game. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "How many?" and watch. Children: Child counts and answers.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and highest number counted. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Tally stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use large counters and foam dice.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use numbers to ten.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to count to thirty.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: makes tally marks; counts in fives; counts to 20; plays counting games.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 5
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep counting and tallying at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child tallies and counts to twenty" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
